title: James Gunn Gives a Fan's DC Timeline a Thumbs-Up — Almost
summary: Keeping track of the DC Universe just got a little easier, thanks to a fan. A user called comicbookcollide posted a list of DC films and TV shows on Threads, arranging them into a timeline of events inside the story world. DC Studios co-head James Gunn replied, "Timelines give me anxiety, but I think this is pretty good." It is about as strong a thumbs-up as a fan timeline can get, though Gunn stopped short of calling it fully official. The timeline places the new film "Clayface" as the second DC Universe project, with its events set in 2021. It also includes "Blue Beetle," the 2023 film that originally belonged to the older DC Extended Universe. Gunn has confirmed that "Blue Beetle" counts as part of the new DC Universe, and the timeline puts its events in 2023, just before "Creature Commandos" Season 1, the official first DC Universe project. That also places "Blue Beetle" after "Clayface," "The Suicide Squad" and "Peacemaker" Season 1, and before "Superman." Gunn has been careful not to endorse the timeline as completely accurate. He has said that "Blue Beetle" needs a few small changes, called retcons, to fit into the new universe, and the same is true of "Peacemaker" Season 1, whose finale was re-edited to show the Justice Gang instead of the former Justice League. The timeline also leaves out some events, such as "Lanterns" Episode 1, which showed that Earth's first Lantern, Hal Jordan, appeared in 1986 and revealed his identity in 1996, long before the events of "Superman," set in 2025. The Wrap previously reported that Blue Beetle actor Xolo Maridueña is set to appear in Gunn's "Superman" sequel, "Man of Tomorrow," which would firm up the film's place in the new universe.
why_it_matters: Superhero movies are more fun when the stories fit together, and fans love helping to map the universe.
